issues: Crossfade/transition frames at ~1.2s, ~2.2s, and ~4.2s produce overlapping and garbled labels (e.g., 'SistSister_B', 'SistSister_A') and superimposed caption text, violating the clear-labels requirement during those frames. Key scientific states (0.2s prometaphase, 3.2s metaphase alignment, 5.2–7.2s anaphase) are legible, but the transition frames should use a cleaner cut or fade to preserve label readability.

scope_review: Model scope is correctly honored: exactly one duplicated chromosome (one sister-chromatid pair) is shown; molecular cohesin cleavage is explicitly excluded and the caption states '(Molecular cleavage not shown.)'; no cytokinesis, nuclear envelope, or spindle-checkpoint content appears. The single-chromosome instantiation of the 'all chromosomes align' source statement is appropriately delimited.

visible_evidence.observation: Duplicated chromosome (two joined pink bars, Sister_A bottom / Sister_B top) positioned LEFT of the metaphase plate; yellow kinetochore dots on each chromatid; white microtubule lines extend from left and right poles to the respective kinetochores (bipolar attachment). Caption: 'Kinetochores of sister chromatids bind microtubules from opposite poles.' Consistent with prometaphase orientation.
Transition/crossfade frame: chromosome shifting rightward toward the plate; labels and caption text are superimposed and garbled. Scientific content interpretable but labels not clear.
Chromosome now near but slightly left of the metaphase plate; moderate label overlap from residual crossfade. Caption: 'Duplicated chromosome aligns at the metaphase plate.'

Duplicated chromosome centered ON the metaphase plate (vertical gray line passes through the centromeric junction); both kinetochores attached to microtubules from opposite poles; labels clear. Metaphase alignment confirmed.

Transition frame at the plate; caption changes to 'Connection breaks down; existing sisters separate toward opposite poles. (Molecular cleavage not shown.)' Labels partially overlapping due to crossfade.

Two distinct chromatids separated with a visible gap: Sister_A (left) with its kinetochore attached to the left-pole microtubule; Sister_B (right) with its kinetochore attached to the right-pole microtubule. Each is on its respective side of the metaphase plate. Anaphase separation confirmed.
Sister_A moved further toward the left pole; Sister_B moved further toward the right pole. Microtubule attachments maintained. Continuous poleward movement confirmed.

Sister_A near the left pole; Sister_B near the right pole. Both chromatids have traversed most of the distance from the metaphase plate to their destination poles. Movement direction and identity tracking consistent throughout.
